title: Macterm desktop widgets
description: The desktop widgets, in ~/.config/macterm/widgets.yaml. Macterm keeps this file up to date by itself. It writes the file again each time that you add, move, resize or remove a widget, and when you quit. It reads your edits when it starts and before each of its own writes. An entry that you add becomes a widget. When you remove an entry, Macterm removes its widget the next time that it starts.

widgets.description: The widgets, in the order of their creation. Entries have no id. Macterm matches them to its widgets by `name`, then by content, then by position.

name.description: An optional label. Settings → Widgets shows it. When an entry has a name, Macterm can match it after you edit by hand.

size.description: The grid span as COLUMNSxROWS, for example "3x2". A cell is 164pt with a 16pt gap. This is the module of the system widgets. The default is 3x3.

column.description: The grid column of the top-left corner of the widget on the grid of the screen, counted from its left edge (0 is the first). Use it with `row`. Leave out both to put the widget in the middle of the screen. A widget next to another widget, including a system widget, snaps into line with it. macOS lines up its own widgets in groups in the same way.

row.description: The grid row of the top-left corner of the widget, counted from the top of the screen (0 is the first, just under the menu bar).

display.description: The screen that `column` and `row` are on, by the name that System Settings → Displays shows. Macterm always writes it, because the primary display changes with the displays that you plug in. Leave it out for the primary display (the display with the menu bar). If a display is not connected and the widget was on it, the cell stays for the time when the display is connected. If the widget was not on it, Macterm takes the cell on the primary display.

cwd.description: The directory where the shell of the widget starts when it starts fresh (absolute, or with ~ at the start). Leave it out for the home directory. Macterm records it from the live shell of the widget.

run.description: A command that Macterm types into the shell of the widget each time that it starts fresh: when the widget is created, when its shell exits, and when Macterm starts and finds that the session is gone (for example after a restart of the Mac). Macterm records it from what the widget runs, in the same way as for a pinned tab. A widget at its shell prompt keeps the command that it had.
